text: The proposed river location for evaluation was on the Mississippi River, downstream of St. Louis, MO. Bathymetry at this location makes it suitable for the use of the jack-up legs or the internal mooring system after carrying out the corresponding detailed bathymetry analysis. The existence of a busy navigable channel would force the mooring of the vessel closer to the riverbanks, obtaining reduced speeds with respect to those recorded in the middle of the channel. Current speed data was not easily accessible, and data from another FOA (FOA 2080) [4] was employed to characterize it. However, due to confidentiality issues, these values cannot be presented in this report. It can be said that recorded speeds fall under the 4 m/s limit specified in the SOPO. For this location, there is no data available for waves or wind, but due to its geographical location, thresholds imposed by the analysis of the rest of the locations are estimated to cover potential environmental conditions given at this location. 3.2.4 Environmental envelopes An initial environmental envelope was defined and backed up by the analysis described above. Two scenarios were considered: some operational conditions, where the CEC device would be operating, and some survival conditions where, even if environmental conditions are not suitable for energy extraction, it is still possible to stay moored waiting for the next operating window. This condition allows the vessel to be moored when environmental conditions are not ideal for the operation of the CEC device without decommissioning the MTV. These conditions aim to cover all the environmental conditions that could happen at most potential locations across the US, allowing the deployment of the MTV. In principle, the MTV will not be installed in locations where low temperatures during the relevant periods of the year could cause water to become completely iced or floes could exist. If any of these sites were selected, deployment time would be restricted to the warm season. However, to be Final Technical Report 18/57 compatible with some sites in the US (i.e., Maine), ice accretion has been considered for stability evaluations following IMO regulation. 3.3 Certification and US flag MTV has been designed to comply with international and US national regulations, complying with IMO and the US Coast Guard regulations. Different frames of applicability were considered, with parameters like length, gross tonnage, and the nature of travel expected to be made. The MTV has been set as an unrestricted navigation vessel, enabling its operation at sea.
